key_insight: Calibrated XGBoost performed best among the evaluated models for identifying a composite of documented suicide-related outcomes in an age-matched EHR cohort.
clinical_relevance: EHR-derived clinical and social-contextual features may support suicide-related risk research, but these findings do not establish readiness for clinical screening.
method: Grouped MIMIC-IV diagnosis codes into clinically motivated features and a composite suicide-related outcome.
Retained all positive patients and sampled age-matched comparison patients to address imbalance and age-related confounding.
Compared logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost with isotonic calibration; used SHAP for feature interpretation.
evidence_signal: In retrospective MIMIC-IV evaluation, calibrated XGBoost achieved the strongest matched-cohort performance; the abstract reports no numerical metrics.
watch_item: The code-based composite includes ideation and prior behavior, so performance should not be interpreted as validated prediction of future suicide attempts or deaths.
paper_title: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records
